title: Replacing LangChain's Deprecated API Chain with LangGraph: An xkcd API Demo
summary: Ryan Booth rebuilds LangChain's deprecated API chain in LangGraph so an LLM can turn an API spec into live REST calls, using the xkcd API as the demo.
learn: An API chain passes a question and an API spec to an LLM, which finds the right endpoints, builds the request and then interprets the response.
LangChain has deprecated its API chain, so the notebook follows the LangGraph example in the LangChain docs instead.
Booth says sanitizing the API spec is where about 90 percent of the time goes, and a spec too large for the context window needs a RAG pipeline or a step that picks only the relevant endpoints.
The graph has three nodes, call tool, execute tool and call model, and its first query returns the latest xkcd comic, "Asteroid News," published that day.
Booth warns that the model makes real API calls, so exposing DELETE, POST, PUT or PATCH endpoints can break things fast.

A curation node asks GPT-4o mini for the top five xkcd comics on a topic and parses the comic numbers into shared state; Booth chose this over DuckDuckGo or Tavily search because the scraped results were poor.
